item.title: Meta Extends Confidential Computing to AI Glasses with Private Processing
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/meta-private-process-ai-glasses/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790823797609.jpg"/><p>Meta has extended Private Processing to AI glasses, using confidential VMs, trusted execution environments, remote attestation, anonymous credentials, OHTTP routing, and TEE-based storage to process AI workloads and persistent user context in the cloud.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Presentation: How to Find Resilience Bugs in Systems that Don't Exist
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/formal-methods-principles/en/mediumimage/hillel-wayne-medium-1790846078119.jpeg"/><p>Hillel Wayne discusses how formal methods principles - such as property strength, state-space verification, and environment assumptions - help software engineers uncover critical architectural bugs early. He shares practical mental models like "adversarial non-determinism" to reason about concurrency, edge cases, and distributed system failures without needing complex mathematical tools.</p> <i>By Hillel Wayne</i>

item.title: Article: Composable Commerce: Inside Shipt’s Kit Platform
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/shipt-composable-commerce-design-ddd/en/headerimage/shipt-composable-commerce-design-ddd-header-1791812515573.jpg"/><p>Shipt launched its Kits feature, enabling quick assembly of themed grocery bundles for events. The platform architecture lets merchandisers easily create store-aware kits, streamlining previously labor-intensive workflows. It utilizes a flexible model of items, shopping lists, and kits to ensure kits display accurately based on local inventory and customer needs.</p> <i>By Khurshid Hameed</i>

item.title: Google Antigravity SDK Adds Local Model Support for Greater Token Efficiency and Code Privacy
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/antigravity-sdk-local-models/en/headerimage/agent-friendly-android-cli-1791967537412.jpeg"/><p>Google has introduced support for local models in the Antigravity SDK, enabling developers to build and execute agentic workflows directly on their own machines, while retaining the flexibility to mix in cloud-based models for higher-level tasks. This approach gives developers greater control over data privacy, inference costs, network dependencies, and computational workload distribution.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Cloudflares Newly Acquired Vite+ Reaches 1.0 with GitLab CI Support, Hooks, and tsup Migration
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-viteplus-stable/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791892196672.jpg"/><p>VoidZero has launched Vite+ 1.0, the first stable version of its JavaScript toolchain. It features a command line tool for managing Node.js, package management, and frontend development from a single configuration file. Enhancements include CI integration for GitLab and Docker support. Future updates are planned, focusing on stability and diagnostics.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Backstage 1.55 Adds Scaffolder Task Recovery and Removes Deprecated Catalog APIs
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/backstage-1-55-task-recovery/en/headerimage/header-1791490255579.jpeg"/><p>Backstage 1.55 adds opt-in recovery for Software Template tasks, resuming crashed or timed-out runs from the last completed step. The release also carries breaking changes to the catalog, search and TechDocs, so teams should review their configuration before upgrading to the current 1.55.3 patch.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

item.title: ZCS Command Injection via SNMP Handlers Enables Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/zimbra-command-injection/en/headerimage/headerZimbra-1791879318550.jpg"/><p>A critical remote command execution vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite, identified as CVE-2026-73570, poses risks by allowing unauthorized access to mailbox data and credentials. This flaw, stemming from improper input sanitization, has been actively exploited. Organizations are advised to upgrade to version 10.1.20 or disable susceptible SNMP services to mitigate risks.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

item.title: Production Patterns for Agents, Evals, and LLM Costs: QCon AI New York 2026
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/qcon-ai-newyork-2026-sessionsv2/en/headerimage/qcon-ai-new-york-2026-1791875885339.jpg"/><p>Once AI is in production, code arrives faster than it can be reviewed, token costs rise, evals have to be good enough to act on, and agents need permissions and guardrails. QCon AI New York 2026 (December 15-16) has confirmed sessions from engineers sharing how they handle these constraints.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

item.title: AWS Reworks EventBridge Custom Buses for Enterprise-Scale Event-Driven Architectures
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-eventbridge-scaling/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791474735792.jpg"/><p>AWS has introduced an enhanced Custom Event Bus for Amazon EventBridge, targeting a problem that often emerges when event-driven architectures move beyond a single team or AWS account: the event infrastructure itself becomes fragmented.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Presentation: How Eve Online Leverages Head Based Sampling to Observe "Fun"
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/eve-observability-head-sampling/en/mediumimage/nicholas-herring-medium-1791444748399.jpg"/><p>Nicholas Herring shares how EVE Online tackles distributed tracing and observability across a 20-year-old MMO architecture. He discusses leveraging head-based, dynamic exponential moving average (EMA), and deterministic sampling techniques to maintain high system fidelity, control telemetry costs, and avoid performance degradation under high-throughput real-time game simulations.</p> <i>By Nicholas Herring</i>

item.title: Cloudflare’s OHTTP Gateway Refuses to Decrypt Requests That Arrive through Cloudflare
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-ohttp-gateway/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791773464365.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has opened a closed beta of its OHTTP Gateway, a managed endpoint that decrypts Oblivious HTTP requests for an origin. The design choice drawing attention is a refusal: the Gateway will not decrypt requests arriving from Cloudflare Workers or from hosts proxied through Cloudflare, because that would put client identifiers and request contents in the same hands.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Cloudflare’s OHTTP Gateway Refuses to Decrypt Requests That Arrive through Cloudflare
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-ohttp-gateway/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791773464365.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has opened a closed beta of its OHTTP Gateway, a managed endpoint that decrypts Oblivious HTTP requests for an origin. The design choice drawing attention is a refusal: the Gateway will not decrypt requests arriving from Cloudflare Workers or from hosts proxied through Cloudflare, because that would put client identifiers and request contents in the same hands.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Spotify More Than Doubled Monthly Code Changes as AI Accelerated Development
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Spotify reports that AI-assisted development more than doubled monthly merged changes, prompting a review of quality and reliability controls across its engineering organization. The company describes changes to testing, observability, rollback capacity, workload prioritization, and automated maintenance as it adapts to higher software change volume.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Article: When Should You Use Liquid Clustering? Benchmarking Lakehouse Layout Strategies
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/liquid-clustering-lakehouse-layout/en/headerimage/liquid-clustering-lakehouse-layout-header-1791465984987.jpg"/><p>Physical data layout is one of the most consequential decisions in lakehouse engineering. The author compares Liquid Clustering, ZOrdering, and partitioning across four workload types on Delta Lake, uncovering two undocumented failure modes that likely affect production systems today and offering a decision framework for choosing the right layout strategy.</p> <i>By Kushal Kumar Vishwakarma</i>

item.title: Podcast: What Does It Really Mean To Program With AI: A Conversation with Joy Ebertz
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/what-really-mean-program-ai/en/smallimage/infoq-podcast-500-1791359941231.jpg"/><p>In this podcast, Michael Stiefel spoke to Joy Ebertz about how the use of artificial intelligence is changing the way architects and developers do their jobs. Focusing on the long term success of the business is one of the most neglected tasks of an architect. This task becomes particularly important as the nature of artificial intelligence changes the landscape of software development.</p> <i>By Joy Ebertz</i>

item.title: Presentation: You Can't Trust Your AI Bill. And Neither Can I
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-cloud-cost-economics/en/mediumimage/erik-peterson-medium-1791451373591.jpg"/><p>Erik Peterson discusses why AI spend is eclipsing cloud bills, triggering a major software engineering cost crisis. He explains tokenmaxxing, unit economics, forced developer promotions, and why fully autonomous AI will write, deploy, and govern code by 2028.</p> <i>By Erik Peterson</i>

item.title: React 19.3: Adds a browser() API, Giving Client-Only Rendering a First-Class Name
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/react-19-3-browser-api/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791791785119.jpg"/><p>React 19.3 was released on September 9, introducing several features including the react-dom browser() API. This API allows components to opt out of server-side rendering, addressing issues with components that rely on client-specific data. It provides a cleaner solution for managing hydration mismatches and supports conditional data fetching, enhancing flexibility for developers.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: GitLab 19.4 Adds Goal-Driven Agents and Tighter Cost Controls
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/gitlab-19-4-goal-driven-agents/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791743492913.jpg"/><p>GitLab has released version 19.4 of its DevSecOps platform, adding a goal-driven mode to GitLab Duo CLI, three hosted open-weight models, a larger set of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and more detailed controls for AI spending.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: Foresight AI Brings Gremlin Agents to Reliability Engineering
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/gremlin-foresight-ai/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791653267864.jpg"/><p>Reliability management company Gremlin has announced the general availability of Foresight AI, an agentic product that analyses services for potential failures, recommends changes and reruns tests to check that a fix works.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: AWS Introduces Enhanced Custom Event Buses for EventBridge
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-enhanced-eventbridge-buses/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790663976977.jpg"/><p>AWS recently announced enhanced custom event buses for Amazon EventBridge, allowing organizations to share a centralized bus across accounts with ordered delivery, simplified subscriber management, event replay, content-based deduplication, and a new publisher/subscriber-based pricing model.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Cloudflare Traces Turns the Proxy Layer into OpenTelemetry Spans, with New Volume-Based Pricing
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-traces-open-beta/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791443919168.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has put Traces into open beta, extending automatic tracing from Workers to security rules, transformations, cache, routing and origin handling as OpenTelemetry spans. Traces accept and forward W3C traceparent headers, and Trace Rules allow targeted sampling. Pricing moves to ingestion and retention volume from December 1.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: CircleCI Makes Machine Runner Orchestrator Generally Available
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/circleci-machine-runner/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790836191409.jpg"/><p>CircleCI has made its Machine Runner Orchestrator 1.0.0 generally available, providing automated scaling of self-hosted machine runner virtual machines according to CI workload demand.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Presentation: Ontology‐Driven Observability: Building the E2E Knowledge Graph at Netflix Scale
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/netflix-observability-aiops-ontology-scale/en/mediumimage/medium-1790845339712.jpg"/><p>Prasanna Vijayanathan and Renzo Sanchez-Silva share how Netflix tackles observability across 38M events/sec. They discuss replacing reactive monitoring with an AI-driven operational ontology and agentic workflows using Claude and graph databases. They explain how unifying MELT telemetry into queryable knowledge graphs enables automated triaging, root-cause analysis, and self-healing systems.</p> <i>By Prasanna Vijayanathan, Renzo Sanchez-Silva</i>

item.title: HashiCorp Relased Terraform Google Cloud Provider 8.0 in General Availability
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/terraform-google-cloud-provider/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791470649216.jpg"/><p>HashiCorp has announced the general availability of version 8.0 of the Terraform provider for Google Cloud. The major release updates the default load balancing for two Compute Engine resources. It also removes resources linked to retired Google Cloud services.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: Cloudflare K2 Builds Event Streams on R2 Object Storage, at a Second of Produce Latency
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-k2-serverless-streams/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791040228747.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has launched K2 in public beta, a serverless event streaming service implementing a durable log on R2 object storage. Cloudflare states produce latency of about one second at p99; a tester reported end-to-end p99 of 7.5 seconds, which a commenter answering for the team said was higher than expected. Consume charges match produce charges per GB.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Presentation: The Reinvention of the Dev Team
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/agentic-dev-teams/en/mediumimage/medium-1790242915891.jpeg"/><p>Hannah Foxwell shares how the surge of agentic coding forces engineering leaders to rethink team dynamics. She discusses three key anchors for navigating AI-driven velocity: building software worth building, prioritizing automated safety over speed, and preserving the human element through generalist "broken comb" skillsets and sustainable on-call practices.</p> <i>By Hannah Foxwell</i>
